case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 05.12.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4804 of 2010 & 1378 of 2011)
full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. Identical questions of law are involved in all these appeals, and therefore, these appeals are disposed of analogously by this judgment. In order to avoid duplication of facts, we are narrating the facts in Civil Appeal No.88 of 2013 which arose from a judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.480 of 2010 for convenience.

<u>2. Writ-petitioners-respondents have been working as Social Welfare Officers under the Directorate of Social Welfare. They have challenged the inaction of the writ-respondents to regularize the service of the writ-petitioners long after 21 years of their recruitment. They also challenged rule 5 of the Gazetted posts (Department of Social Welfare) Recruitment Rules, 1979 relating to the determination of regularization and seniority of the officers, who have been transferred from development project to the revenue budget. The writ-respondents non-feasance for long 21 years after the writ-petitioners-respondents joined the service, without any reason, is ultra vires rule 5 of the Rules, 1979. The writ-petitioners, after fulfilling all the criteria specified in the notice of appointment, applied for the posts of Upazila Social Welfare Officer and after successfully passing in all the tests, got appointment on ad-hoc basis. They were appointed on different dates in 1975. When the activities of the project came to an end, writ-respondent No.1, by its Memo dated 4th December, 2001 absorbed the writ-petitioners in the revenue budget with effect from 1st July, 1995. The writ-petitioners were shifted from a temporary development project to permanent revenue budget because their efficiency, competence and proficiency. After that, writ-respondent No.2, by its Memo dated 3rd February, 2005, requested the writ-respondent No.1 to regularize the service of the writ-petitioners through the Public Service Commission. In the said letter, writ-respondent No.2 admitted the fact that the writ-petitioners have been serving the government for last 20 years and that it is extremely necessary to regularize their service according to SRO dated 2nd May, 1995, through the Public Service Commission (PSC). Writ-respondent No.2 recommended 46 officers, including the writ-petitioners and con-firmed that no case either departmental or criminal, was pending against them. After that, the PSC, by its letter dated 2nd August, 2006, recommended 26 (twenty six) officers, including the writ-petitioner before writ-respondents No.1 for regularizing in the service. Writ-respondent No.1, by its Memo dated 28th August, 2006, regularized some of the writ-petitioners, long after 21 years of their service. The PSC again recommended 18 (eighteen) other officers, including the writ-petitioners for regularization. After receiving the said recommendation from PSC, writ-respondent No.1 regularized the service of the officers in 1995 whose names have been recommended, yet they were not regularized in the service until 2006.</u>

3. The writ-respondents refrained from doing so, knowing fully well that their seniority would be counted from the date of regularization according to rule 5 of the Rules relating to the determination of the seniority of the officers who have been transferred from development project to revenue budget. As per rule 5 of the Rules, the seniority of any officer appointed under this rule will be counted from the date of his regularization in the service. The writ petitioners were regularized in 2006 and 'as such, their seniority would, as per rule 5 of the Rules be counted from that date. Considering the circumstances, the writ-petitioners, by letter dated 31st December, 2007, requested writ-respondent No.1, to bring necessary amendment to rule 5 of the Rules, so that the writ-petitioner could get equal opportunity with those whose recruitment to the government service was direct, in respect of promotion and other seniority related matters. Writ-respondent No.2 appreciating the necessity amendment, by its letter dated 7th January, 2008, recommended to writ-respondent No. 1. As no step was taken by, writ-respondent No.1 to cause necessary amendment to rule 5, writ-respondent No.2 again, by its letter dated 26th August, 2008, requested writ-respondent No.1 to bring necessary changes in rule 5. Though the writ-respondents themselves have appreciated the fact that rule 5 is absolutely illegal, arbitrary and called for amendment, till date, no step has been taken by the writ-respondents in this regard. The service of the writ-petitioners has been confirmed by writ respondent No.1, by its Memo dated 12th March, 2009, with effect from St June, 2008. The writ-petitioners were given selection grade by writ-respondent No.1, by its Memo dated 22nd November, 2009. A notice of appointment was published in 'The Daily Shangbad on 25th March, 1984, for appointment in the posts of Upazila Social Welfare Officer on ad-hoc basis under the Department of Social Welfare. The failure on the part of the writ-respondents in regularizing the writ-petitioners within a reasonable period is patently against the legitimate expectation of the writ-petitioners and the same is liable to be declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

4. The High Court Division was of the view that the views taken by this court in Bangladesh V. Md. Azizur Rahman, 46 DLR (AD) 19 is applicable in this case and the ratio decided in that case is that for the purpose of the computation of seniority, if the dates of original entry of the writ petitioners into the government service shall be treated as the decisive date but rule 5 of Rules of 2005 provides that the seniority can be counted from the date of regularization and that rule 5 cannot have stand on the way in giving the seniority of the writ petitioners from the date of their appointment. The High Court Division set aside rule 5 of Rules of 2005.

5. Before considering the points of law, we would like to reproduce the terms of the rule issued by the High Court Division which is relevant for our consideration and the same is as under: "Let a Rule Nisi be issued, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents failure to regularize the service the petitioners until 2006, i.e. even after 21 years of their recruitment, shall not declared to have been without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and also as to why regulation 5 of the Regulation, dated 20.06.2005, relating to the determination of the Regularization and Seniority of the officers, who have been transferred from Development project to Revenue Budget (Annexure-A), read with the Rule 6 of the gazetted post (Department of Social Welfare), Recruitment Rules, 1979 (Annexure-B), shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect."

<u>6. The first question is whether writ petitioners can get any relief as per terms of the rule nisi. They made a prayer which itself is not in conformity with law and in terms of the rule they are not entitled to the relief sought. The first part of the rule is relating to their regularisation in service in 2006. The second limb of the prayer is their regularisation in service after 21 of recruitment is unlawful. The third limb of their prayer is rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 in determining their seniority and that of rule 6 of Rules, 1979 should be declared unlawful. The procedure for regularisation in respect of the employees working in the development project has been provided in rule 4 of Rules 2005. In order to claim regularisation in the revenue set up one must satisfy the criteria provided in clauses (ক), (খ), (গ) of sub-rule (1) of rule 4 and then the recommendation of PSC will be necessary if the post in which the officer wants to enter requires recommendation. The writ petitioners right of regularisation has been recognised in 2005 and they have been regularised in 2006 after compliance of formalities. If their regularisation in 2006 is declared illegal, how they can claim seniority over 'others is not clear to us. Secondly unless the writ petitioner makes substantive relief, how the court will give them the status or entitlement in office they claimed? The language of the rule issuing order presupposes that the writ petitioners have challenged the constitutionality of rule 5 of the “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেট পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরন ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারন বিধিমালা, ২০০৫” along with rule 6 of the Rules, 1979.</u>

<u>7. These Rules have been promulgated by the President in exercise of powers conferred under article 133 of the constitution by gazette notification dated 28th June, 2005. Rule 5 which is relevant for our consideration is reproduced below:</u>

<u>“৫। জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণঃ</u>

<u>(১০) এই বিধিমালার অধীন কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণের ক্ষেত্রে তাহার চাকুরী নিয়মিতকরণের  তারিখ হইতে গণনা করা হইবে।</u>

<u>(২) কোন উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে একই তারিখে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত একাধিক কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর জ্যৈষ্ঠতা নিম্নরুপ নির্ধারিত হইবে, যথাঃ-</u>

<u>(ক) উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে নিয়োগের সময় সংশিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ কতৃক প্রস্তুতকৃত মেধা তালিকা বা প্রদত্ত নম্বরের গ্রেডিং যদি থাকে, এর ভিত্তিতে</u>

<u>(খ) দফা (ক) এ উল্লিখিত তালিকা বা প্রদত্ত নম্বরের গ্রেডিং না থাকিলে সেই ক্ষেত্রে নূন্যতম শিক্ষাগত যোগ্যতা অর্জনের বৎসরের ভিত্তিতে এবং উক্ত বৎসর একই বৎসর হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে বয়সের ভিত্তিতে ।</u>

<u>(৩) কোন উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প পূর্বে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্রের অভাবে, পদাধিকারীর ক্রটির কারণে নয়, একই পদে পরে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর পূর্বে বা একই সংঙ্গে নিয়মিত না হইয়া পরবর্তী সময়ে নিয়মিত হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে পরে নিয়মিত হওয়া সত্তেও পর্বে নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর উপর তাহার জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে।</u>

<u>(৪) একাধিক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে একই পদে দুই বা ততোধিক কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীকে নিয়মিত করা হইলে সেই ক্ষেত্রে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে যোগদানের তারিখ একই হইলে সেই ক্ষেত্রে বয়জ্যেষ্ঠতার ভিত্তিতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে।</u>

<u>(৬) নিয়মিতভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর নিয়োগের তারিখ বা নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা; কর্মচারীর নিয়মিতকরণের তারিখ একই হইলে সেক্ষেত্রে নিয়মিতভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা; কর্মচারীগণ নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীগণের উপর জ্যেষ্ঠতা পাইবে।</u>

<u>a) It provides, in determining the seniority of the officers and employees under the Rules from the date of regularization;</u>

<u>(2) In regularising more officers or employees who were appointed in the development project on the same day, the determination of seniority will be decided in the following manner;</u>

<u>In accordance with merit list or grading number, if any, prepared by the authority at the time of appointment in the development project; In the absence of the above, on the basis of the year of educational qualification, and if the year of educational qualification is same„ on the basis of age; In the absence of requisite documents of any officers or employees working in the project without his faults, even if there is regularization in respect of the same post prior or later on jointly, such employee or officer shall get seniority over the officer or employee who has been regularised earlier on the basis of appointment in the development project. If two or more officers or employees are regularized from different projects, their seniority will be decided on the basis of joining in the development project; (5) In case of regularization of two or more officers or employees in the same post from different development projects, and if their joining in the development project is same, their seniority will be counted according to their age; (6) If the date of appointment of an officer or employee on regular basis and the regularization of an officers or employee is made on the same day, the regular officer or employee shall get seniority over the officer or employee regularized in the revenue set up.</u>

8. These Rules have been promulgated for the first time taking into consideration of the anomaly created in the process of absorption of an officer or employee in the revenue set up from the development' project. Before promulgation of such rule, the officers and employees employed, in the development projects had no claim of right of absorption in the revenue set up because of the fact that they were appointed purely on temporary basis for a limited period without reserving any right of future appointment. These development projects were undertaken just immediately after the independence of the country with the grants given by different donor agencies. It is noticed that even after completion of the development projects, the services of those officers or employees had been retained for various reasons. Sometimes the donor agencies extended the projects for further period and sometimes the government collected funds from different sources and continued those projects. This will be evident from the definition of

২ (ক)উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পস্থ অর্থ ৯ এপ্রিল, ১৯৭২ খ্রিষ্টাব্দ হইতে ৩০ জুন, ১৯৯৭ খ্রিষ্টাব্দ তারিখ পর্যন্ত সময়ের মধ্যে শুরু হওয়া সরকার অনুমোদিত, উন্নয়ন বাজেটভুক্ত প্রকল্পসমূহ।

(খ) ‘উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের চাকুরিকালস্থা' অর্থ কোন উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে যোগদানের তারিখ হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটের পদে সাময়িকভাবে পদস্থ হওয়া পর্যন্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীর চাকুরী কাল।

(গ) “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী” অর্থ ১৯৭২ সনের এপ্রিল মাসের ৯ তারিখ হইতে ৩০ শে জুন, ১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখের মধ্যে শুরু হওয়া উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের কোন পদে স্কেলভিত্তিতে নিযুক্ত কর্মচারী এবং ১৯৮৩ সনের মে মাসের ১৩ তরিখ বা তৎপরবর্তীকালে রাজস্ব বাজেটের কোন পদে সাময়িকভাবে পদস্থ কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী”

<u>9. This definition and explanations suggest make that the officers or employees who have been appointed in the development projects, if their services have been temporarily approved in the revenue set up, their services will be counted only from the date of joining in the development project till the date they have been regularized temporarily in the revenue budget. So, these officers or employees could not claim as of right of regularization till the promulgation of the Rules by SRO 182 dated 28th June, 2005. Their regularization will be made subject to the availability of vacant posts in the revenue set up otherwise even after promulgation of the Rules, they cannot claim as of right to be regularized in the revenue set up. They will be given seniority from the date of their regularization and if more employees are regularized on the same date, the criteria has been delineated on the basis of efficiency, gradation, qualification, age, etc. etc.</u>

10. Even if one employee is appointed on regular basis and another employee's service has been regularized for the development project on the same day, though the employee who has been appointed in the development project is senior on the point of his joining in the service, he will not get seniority because of the fact that his service has been regularized on the same day with a regular employee, that is to say, the regular employee shall get seniority over an employee whose service has been regularized. There is no ambiguity in the language used in rule 5 and the court cannot give any meaning other than the meaning as may be discerned on a plain reading of rule 5.

11. Generally speaking when a language of a statute is plain and ambiguous, the court is required to give effect to the word used in the statute irrespective of its consequences. It is not open to a court to adopt a hypothetical construction on the ground that such construction is more consistent with the object and policy of the statute. If the language of a statute is clear, it must be enforced though the result may be harsh, unfair or inconvenient. The court cannot substitute the plain words so as to limit the application of the statute. The court is bound to give the effect to the statute irrespective of consequences. To add to the above, if the language of the statute is found plain and unambiguous and admits of only one meaning, no question of construction of statute arises as the statute speaks for itself. Reference in this connection are the cases of Gurudevadatt V. Maharashtra, AIR 2001 SC 1980, Nathi Devi V. Radha Devi, AIR 2005 SC 648, Solicitor V. Syed Sanwar Ali, 27 DLR (AD) 16.

12. Mr. Roukan Uddin Mahmud, learned Counsel appearing for the respondents argues that if rule 5 is read together with rules 6, there will be no confusion in coming to the conclusion that the seniority of an officer or employee after regularization should be computed from the date of joining irrespective of the date of regularization in the revenue set up Rule 6 read as follows:

(৬) ‘উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের চাকুরিকাল গণনাঃ নিয়মিতকৃত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে চাকুরীকাল তাহার বেতন, ছুটি, পেনশন ও আনুষাঙ্গিক সুবিধাদি নির্ধারণের ক্ষেত্রে গণনা করা হইবে।

13. It provides that for determining the period of service in respect of an officer or employee whose service has been regularized, the scale, leave, pension and related benefits shall be determined fi.om the date of joining in the development project. This rule relates to counting the period of service for the purpose of giving financial benefits to an employee, whose service has been regularized from the development project. It may be said that it is in the nature of consolatory provision giving some extra largesse" by the government to those who have been contributing to the nation without reservation of any status for such contributions. This rule has no nexus with rule 5, and both these rules have been included with different objects and purposes. This rule does not supersede rule 5, which has provided the procedure of counting the seniority of those who are regularised from the development projects. The procedure for regularisation is provided in rule It is only after the fulfillment of the criteria provided in rule 4, if an officer or employee is regularised, his seniority will be determined in accordance with rule 5.

14. There is always a presumption of constitutionality of a statute and the burden lies upon the person who challenges the constitutionality of the statute or a provision of it is to show that there has been a transgression of the constitutional principles. Reference in this connection is the cases of S. A. Sabur V. Retiring officer, 41 DLR (AD) 30 and Prabhu as V. India, AIR 1966 S.C. 1044. An Act of, Parliament will be validated only in the event of certain circumstances exist, it will be presumed that all such circumstances do exist. Where the classification embodied in a legislation is under challenge, if any state of facts can be reasonably conceived that would sustain it, the existence of such state of facts must be assumed. It must be presumed that the legislature understands and correctly appreciates the need of the people that its laws are directed to problems made manifest by experience and that its discriminations are based on adequate grounds. In this connection references may be made the cases of New York Rapid Transist Corporation V. New York, (1937) 303 US 573; Ram Krisna Dalmia V. Justice Talukder, AIR 1958 S.C. 538, and S.A. Saur (ibid). A person challenging the validity of a statute must come out with clear pleadings demonstrating that the differentia of the classification contained in the law/statute have no reason-able nexus with any legitimate governmental objective and must adduce evidence in support of the pleadings. There is no pleading at all to declare rule 5 unconstitutional or inconsistency with any law.

15. The issue involved in this appeal is the determination of seniority of an officer or employee of development project whose service has been regularised and the determination of his status with those working in the revenue set up. It is not an issue to determine the seniority on the basis of benefits to be payable to an officer or employee whose service has been regularized in, the development project. It is true that if an employee's tenure of service is counted from the date of joining in the development project, such employee will get much higher financial benefits than an officer or employee whose service has been regularised later on. There is, there-fore, some inconsistency in these two pro-visions but for this reason rule 5 cannot be declared unconstitutional. Mr. Mahmud submits that a harmonious interpretation may be given in this 4 respect that if an employee gets higher salary and his length service is higher than a regular officer or employee, the seniority should be counted from the date of joining in the service, otherwise a senior employee who is getting higher salary will be compelled to serve under a junior officer/employee with much humiliation which is unethical. We find no force in the contention 'of the learned Counsel and this is not a legal ground to declare a law unconstitutional.

16. It has been held in Beaman V. A.R.T.S. (1949) 1 KB 550, where a word has been construed judicially in a certain legal area, it is right to give it in the same meaning if it occurs in a statute dealing with the same general subject-matter, unless the context makes it clear that the word must have a different construction. However, this presumption will not be available when the same words are used in different context. The same word may be used in different senses in the same statute and even in the same section. The usual reason for attributing different meanings to the same word is simply that it occurs in different contexts. Rule 5 has been given in one context and rule 6 has been given in different context. These two provisions cannot be equated nor the word can supersede the other. The High Court Division has committed a fundamental error in presuming that rule 5 will not stand in the way in giving the seniority to the writ petitioner relying the views taken in Md. Azizur Rahman, 46 DLR (AD) 19.

17. The High Court Division is totally misconceived in presuming as such. As observed above, a law cannot be avoided by a court of law if on a plain reading of the statute the words used in it expresses the intention of the legislature and words should be interpreted in their ordinary and natural meaning. The primary function of a court of law being jus dicere non jus dare i.e. to declare the law, not to make the law. The paramount rule of interpretation of legislative intent should be applied by the court (commissioner of Sale Tax V. Parson Tools (1975) 4 SCC 22.) If the law is found not conformity with the fundamental rights guaranteed in part III of the constitution, the court can declare a law to be ultra vires the constitution, otherwise not. Article 26 of the constitution provides "All existing law inconsistent with the provisions of this Part shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, become void on the commencement of this Constitution'. So, it is to be looked into whether rule 5 of Rules 2005 is inconsistent with articles 27 or 29(1) of the Constitution. Though the High Court Division noticed articles 27 and 29, it has not assigned any reason why this rule 5 is inconsistent with articles 27 and 29(1) of the Constitution. True, the constitution expressly conferred upon the High Court Division the power of judicial review and if it finds that any statute is inconsistent with the constitution, it can declare the said statute ultra vires the constitution to the extent it is found inconsistency.

18. A law may be declared ultra vires the constitution if it is in contravention of the fundamental rights guaranteed in part III of the Constitution. He must show that his right or interest has been affected by reason of the statute. But a particular provision or section of a statute is found inconsistent with another provision of the same statute, how the court can declare one pro-vision/section ultra vires article 27 or 29(1) of the constitution?

19. As observed above, there is presumption in favour of the constitutionality of an enactment and the person who claims the statute unconstitutional must show that there has been a clear transgression of the constitutional principles. The High Court Division did not even declare rule 5 ultra vires article 27 or 29(1). It simply set aside rule 5. Assuming that it has declared rule 5 ultra vires the constitution, how declare the said statute ultra vires the constitution to the extent it is found inconsistency. A law may be 'declared ultra vires the constitution if it is in contravention of the fundamental rights guaranteed in part III of the Constitution. He must show that his right or interest has been affected by reason of the statute. But a particular provision or section of a statute is found inconsistent with another provision of the same statute, how the court can declare one provision section ultra vires article 27 or 29(1) of the constitution?

20. As observed above, there is presumption in favour of the constitutionality of an enactment and the person who claims the statute unconstitutional must show that there has been a clear transgression of the constitutional principles. The High Court Division did not even declare rule 5 ultra vires article 27 or 29(1). It simply set aside rule 5. Assuming that it has declared rule 5 ultra vires the constitution, how the officers/employees will get seniority over others who are already in the revenue set up. It will create anomaly. It is the only a provision which gives a guideline to count the seniority of an officer or employee working in the development project whose service has been regularized in the revenue budget and he can claim the seniority from the date of regularization. If this rule 5 is struck down the writ petitioners cannot claim any right of seniority but rule 6 does not relate to determine the seniority.

21. The High Court Division has totally failed to comprehend the ratio in Azizur Rahman. The said case has no manner of application, inasmuch as, in that case the question was for determination of seniority in terms of rules 4, 5, 6 of the BCS Seniority Rules, 1983. In that case, the vires of the Bangladesh Ad-hoc Appointees (Counting and Determination of Seniority) Rules, 1990 was challenged. By these Rules seniority of the ad-hoc appointees is to be counted from the date of their original appointment on ad-hoc basis but their seniority was to be counted under the Rules in force from the date of their regular appointment on the recommendation of PSC. The writ petitioner Md. Azizur Rahman was placed third position in merit while the writ respondents were placed below him. Writ respondent No.6 who would not qualify in the interview was regularized from 30th June 1983 under the provision of Regularization of Ad-hoc Appointment Rules 1983. Writ petitioner claimed to have acquired a vested right of seniority over the respondents who were placed below him in order of merit by PSC but the government by circular dated 22nd April, 1984, tried to alter this order of seniority and directed that the seniority of the ad-hoc appointees after regularization, would count from the date of ad-hoc appointment. This court held that the impugned Rules have not affected the respondents relating to their conditions of service although their chances of promotion may be affected, which is not a condition of service.

22. Therefore, the issue involved in that case is quite distinguishable. In that case, it was observed, the expression equality before law should not be interpreted in its absolute sense to hold that all persons are equal in all respects disregarding different conditions and circumstances in which they are placed or special quality and characteristics which some of them may possess but which are lacking in others. It has further been observed that the ad-hoc appointments were made and allowed to continue for indefinite period and this classification got reasonable basis having nexus to the object to be achieved, that is, to do justice to these ad-hoc appointees by including in their service, the period they served on ad-hoc basis. This benefit has been e uniformly distributed to all the officers-those who had been regularized earlier through the PSC and those who were regularized under the Ad-hoc Appointment Regularization Rules, 1983. The High Court Division has totally ignored ratio decided in Azizur Rahman's case. More so, it will be seen that from the rule issuing order itself shows that the writ petitioners cannot claim any relief in the manner the writ petition has been drawn. They did not challenge constitutionality of rule 5 and no rule has been issued in that regard. We, find no rational basis to hold the view that rule 5 of Rules of 2005 ultra vires any of the provisions of the constitution. Learned Counsel appearing for the respondents has also failed to point out any inconsistency in the law save and except the inconsistency shown between rules 5 and 6. As observed above, for this inconsistency rule 5 cannot be declared ultra vires, inasmuch as, these two rules have been included in the Rules under two different premises. One is for determining the procedure of seniority and the other is for determining the period of service from the purpose of giving benefits to the employees whose services have been regularized in the revenue set up.

23. Civil Appeal Nos.89, 90, 91, 92, 93, 94 and 95 of 2013 arose out of Writ Petition Nos.2729 of 2012, 4804 of 2010, 1378 of 2011. The rules were issued to the effect that why the writ petitioners should not be directed to be regularized in their respective posts from the date of joining.

24. How the court will give such relief in presence of rule 5 of Rules of 2005 unless it is shown that this rule ultra vires any of the provisions of the constitution. The writ petitioners could not make out such a case in their writ petitions. Their only claim is that they were appointed long before they were regularized, and therefore, they were legally entitled to be regularized earlier. Their right of regularization has been recognized only on 28th June, 2005, and therefore, they cannot claim their seniority with retrospective effect. A plain reading of the Rules clearly shows that rule 5 is in prospective effect. It cannot be given retrospective effect. In Azizur Rahman also this court held in paragraph 43 that the Public Service Commission Rules, 1990 which governed all classes of appointments either direct or ad-hoc appointees are not retrospective because the same will be applicable to the employees covered by the said Rules from the date of making thereof and in the said Rules there is no element of retrospectivity.

25. It further held in Azizur Rahman that Rule 7(1) of the impugned Rules of 1990, gives recognition of the gradation list pre-pared under the Circular dated 22.4.84 and the gradation list if prepared earlier will be subject to the said rules and shall be deemed to have been made under the said Rules. If no gradation list has been pre-pared earlier in any cadre then a fresh gradation list will be prepared in conformity with the provision of impugned rules of 1990. Therefore, Rule 7(1) of the impugned Rules of 1990 is also prospective. It also appears that the Ad-hoc appointees enjoyed the benefits of continuous service such as leave, increments, etc. from the date of ad-hoc appointment till the making of the impugned Rules of 1990. Hence, the impugned Rules of 1990 have not altered the condition's of service, pertaining to seniority with retrospective effect and the said rules are not retrospective. These impugned Rules being prospective in operation the same will govern seniority from the date of making thereof and it cannot be argued that the said Rules have affected any vested right i.e. the promotion, if any, already earned. The impugned Rules of 1990 have given protection to it in Rules 7(2) thereof.

26. Therefore, it is very difficult to approve the views taken by the High Court Division that the seniority of the writ petitioners can be given retrospective effect. On perusal of the writ petitions and the judgments we have noticed that there was delay in the process of regularization in Writ Petition No.4804 of 2010. The writ petitioners are claiming their seniority since 1985. In Writ Petition No.1378 of 2011, the writ petitioners are claiming their seniority since 1997. So writ petitioners claim their seniority with retrospective effect from the day of their joining in the development projects. There was no law conferring any right of regularization who were appointed in development projects when they were appointed. If they have acquired no right on the day of their appointment, how can they claim seniority from the date as of right? Unless they have acquired a right, they cannot challenge the vires of the law only because they were appointed earlier. The writ petitioners have accrued no right and therefore, the writ petitions are not legally maintainable. The High Court Division has totally ignored that aspect of the matter.

27. The appeals, are therefore, allowed without any order as to costs.

28. Nazmun Ara Sultana, I have the privilege to go through the draft copy of the judgment written by my Lord Chief Justice. With due respect I differ with the findings and decision arrived at by my Lord Chief Justice in this judgment and as such I am writing a separate judgment giving my decision assigning reasons thereof.

29. All these civil appeals have arisen out of the judgments passed by the High Court Division in different writ petitions making the Rules absolute. In those writ petitions the writ petitioners challenged the inaction of the authority to regularize their service in the revenue budget after their absorption there from the development, projects within unusual long period and also challenged the constitutionality / validity of Rule 5 of “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫” (hereinafter referred to as Rules of 2005).

30. The cases of all the writ-petitioners in all the writ-petitions are similar. All the writ petitioners were initially recruited by the Government for different Development projects and after the end of those projects they were all absorbed in the revenue budget long several years before. The writ petitioners have alleged in their respective writ petition to the effect that they made several representations to the authority to regularize their service but the authority did not take any initiative to that effect. That the respondent No.2, the Director General, Directorate of Social Welfare vide memo dated 03.02.2005 requested the respondent No.1 to regularize the service of the writ petitioners through the Public Service Commission, and in the said letter the respondent No.2 admitted the fact that the writ petitioners were serving in the Government employment for last 20 years and it was extremely necessary to regularize their service according to the dictate contained in the S.R.O. dated 02.05.1995. That at last, in the year 2006 only, the respondent No.1, after obtaining the recommendation from Public Service Commission, regularized the service of the writ petitioners in several phases. The writ petitioners have alleged that they were absorbed in the Government revenue budget in the year 1995, yet they were not regularized in the service until 2006, that this was out and out illegal on the part of the respondents; that the respondents refrained from regularizing the writ petitioners service within a reasonable time knowing fully well that their seniority will be counted from the date of regularization according to rule 5 of the Rules of 2005.

31. The writ petitioners have challenged the validity of rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 also and have stated that they requested the respondent No.1 by sending letters through the respondent No.2 to bring necessary amendments to this rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 and the respondent No.2 also, appreciating the necessity of this amendment, forwarded that letter of the writ petitioners with recommendation to the respondent No.1, but no step was taken by the respondent No.1 to bring necessary amendment to rule 5 of the Rules of 2005. That the respondent No. 2 again vide his letter dated 26.08.2008 requested the respondent No.1 to bring necessary change in that rule 5. The writ petitioners have contended also that though the respondents themselves 'have appreciated that the rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 is absolutely illegal, arbitrary and call for amendment, but till date no step has been taken by the respondents to amend the same.

32. The High Court Division issued Rules Nisi in all the Writ Petitions. One of those Rules is quoted below: "Let a Rule Nisi be issued, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents' failure to regularize the service of the petitioners until 2006, i.e. even after 21 years of their recruitment, shall not be declared to have been without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and also as to why regulation 5 of the Regulation, dated 20.06.2005, relating to the determination of the regularisation and seniority of the officers, who have been transferred from Development project to Revenue Budget (Annexure-A), read with Rule 6 of the gazetted post (Department of Social Welfare), recruitment Rules, 1979 (Annexure-B), shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect."

33. The respondents contested the Rules by filing affidavit-in-opposition.

34. Different Division Benches of the High Court Division, after hearing the learned Advocates of both the sides made those rules absolute by different judgments. In one of those judgments the High Court Division made observations thus, clause 5, cannot have a leg to stand on, and the same, in its present form, is hence liable to be effaced, because unamended rule 5 stands as a stumbling block against this claim of the petitioners."

35. The High Court Division, however, relying on the case of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Azizur Rahman reported in 46 DLR (AD) 19 held that "for the purpose of the computation of seniority, date of the original entry of the petitioner into the Government job should be treated as the decisive date. But, as admitted, clause 5 of the Rules of 2005, stands as a hurdle, because under that clause seniority can be computed from the date of regularization not from the date of initial entry. Hence, we entertain the view that the petitioners are entitled to have their seniority computed from that date, not from the date of regularization".

36. However, in these appeals,' the most important question which needs determination is whether rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 can be treated as a valid one or it should be adjudicated as ultra vires Constitution. For convenience of discussion we need to quote the entire rule 5 of this Rules of 2005 here,

৫। জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ । - (১) এই বিধিমালার অধীন নিয়মিতকৃত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণের ক্ষেত্রে তাহার চাকুরী নিয়মিতকরনের তারিখ হইতে গণনা করা হইবে।

(২) কোন উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে একই তারিখে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত একাধিক কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর জ্যেষ্ঠতা নিম্নরুপে নির্ধারিত হইবে, যথাঃ

(ক) উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে নিয়োগের সময় সংশিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক প্রস্তুতকৃত মেধা তালিকা বা প্রদত্ত নম্বরের গ্রেডিং যদি থাকে, এর ভিত্তিতে;

(খ) দফা (ক) এ উল্লিখিত তালিকা বা প্রদত্ত নম্বরের গ্রেডিং না থাকিলে সেইক্ষেত্রে ন্যুনতম শিক্ষাগত  যোগ্যতা অর্জনের বৎসরের ভিত্তিতে এবং উক্ত বৎসর একই বৎসর হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে বয়সের ভিত্তিতে ।

(৩) কোন উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে পূর্বে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্রের অভাবে, পদাধিকারীর ক্রটির কারণে নয়, একই পদে ; পরে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর পূর্বে বা এই সঙ্গে নিয়মিত না হইয়া পরবর্তী সময়ে নিয়মিত হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে পরে নিয়মিত হওয়া সত্ত্বেও পূর্বে নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর উপর তাহার জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হবে।

(৪) একাধিক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে একই পদে দুই বা ততোধিক কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীকে নিয়মিত করা হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে যোগদানের  তারিখের ভিত্তিতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে।

(৫) একাধিক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে একই পদে দুই বা ততোধিক কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীকে নিয়মিত করা হইলে এবং তাহাদের য���গদানের তারিখ একই হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে বয়ঃজ্যেষ্ঠতার ভিক্তিতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে।

(৬) নিয়মিতভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর নিয়োগের তারিখ এবং নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর নিয়মিতকরণের তারিখ একই হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে নিয়মিতভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা  কর্মাচরীগণ নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীগণের উপর জ্যেষ্ঠতা পাইবেন।”

37. The clause 1 of the above quoted-rule 5 has ordained that the seniority of any officer or employee, who has been absorbed in the Revenue Budget from the Development project, will be counted from the date of regularization of his service. The procedure for regularization of the service of the employees of Development project absorbed in Revenue Budget has been stated in rule 4 of the Rules of 2005. Clause 3 of this Rule 4 is quoted below:

“৩। কর্মকমিশনের আওতাভুক্ত কোন পদে কমিশনের সুপারিশক্রমে এবং কমিশনের আওতাবহির্ভূত কোন পদে বিভাগীয় পদোন্নতি বা বাছাই কমিটির সুপারিশক্রমে নিয়মিত করিতে হইবে”

38. In view of the above quoted clause 3 of rule and clause 1 of rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 it is evident that the seniority of the employees absorbed in the Revenue setup from Development project is to be counted from the date of regularization of their service in the Revenue set-up and this regularization depends on the recommendation of Public Service Commission or departmental promotion or select committee,' as the case may be. This recommendation of Public Service Commission, undisputedly, is not given within any time limit. It is a matter of common experience that Public Service Commission, in many cases, takes a long period of several years to give its recommendation / opinion for regularization of the employees absorbed in the Revenue setup from Development project. In the present case also, as it has been stated above, the writ petitioners though were absorbed long before in the year 2001 but the Public Service Commission,' only on 02.08.2006 gave its recommendation for the regularization of some of the writ petitioners for the first time. Many cases have come so far to this Court with the same allegation that for the delay of Public Service Commission in giving its recommendation for the regularization of the service of the employees absorbed in Revenue set-up those employees, in spite of having served in the Government service for long period even after their absorption in the revenue set-up, became junior to the employees who were appointed in the Government service long after their appointment and even long after their absorption in the revenue setup. The rule 5 of these Rules of 2005, thus, obviously, is creating not only anomaly but also discrimination among the employees.

For example:

39. A group of employees from Development Project was absorbed in the revenue setup, say, in the year 2006 and thereafter some other group of regular employees were directly appointed in the revenue setup in the year 2007. Now, if some of the employees of the group absorbed in the Revenue setup from Development project are regularized in the service on getting necessary recommendation of the Public Service Commission / Departmental promotion or Select Committee before appointment of the other group of regular employees in the year 2007 they will be senior to those regular employees appointed after their regularization in the service. But the other employees of the said group absorbed in the revenue setup in the year 2006, if regularized after the appointment of that other group of regular employees in the year 2007 they will become junior to those regular employees in spite of being even senior to those other employees of their group who have attained seniority over those regular employee.

40. Thus, obviously, rule 5 of the Rules of 2005 may create, in fact, it is creating discrimination among the employees. For this reasons only, this rule 5 of the Rules of 2005, in my opinion, is ultra vires the Constitution being violative of Article 27 and Article'29(1) of the Constitution. Being absorbed in the revenue setup long before direct appointment of regular employees in the revenue setup and having possibility of being senior to those subsequently appointed employees if any employee is deprived of having that benefit in the service for the reason only of this rule 5(1) of the Rules of 2005 that will be undoubtedly violation of Article 29(1) of the Constitution. So, evidently, the above quoted rule 5(1) of Rules 2005, in its present form, without any guiding clause, may better- be termed as a tool for making discrimination among the employees in the service of Republic.

41. There are other reasons also for making this rule 5 of Rules of 2005 discriminatory and arbitrary. Clause 3 of the Rule 5 runs thus,

(৩) কোন উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পে পূর্বে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারী প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্রের অভাবে, পদাধিকারীর ক্রটির কারণে নয়, একই পদে পর নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর পূর্বে বা এক সঙ্গে নিয়মিত না হইয়া পরবর্তী সময়ে নিয়মিত হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে পরে নিয়মিত হওয়ার সত্ত্বেও পূর্বে নিয়মিতকৃত কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর উপর তাহার জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে ।”

42. This above quoted clause 3 of Rule 5 is, no doubt, good for the employees absorbed in the revenue set-up from the Development project for themselves. But situation may arise creating anomaly in the service when a junior employee of Development project (absorbed in revenue set-up) is regularized before a senior employee of the Development project (absorbed in the revenue set-up) and gets seniority above some regular employees of the revenue setup appointed after his regularization and thereafter, if any other senior employee absorbed in the revenue setup is regularized he will get seniority over that earlier regularized absorbed employee as per this above clause 3 of rule 5. And then what will be the position? Will this senior employee who was regularized subsequently after his junior colleague, in spite of being senior to that colleague get seniority above the regular employee who is junior to his junior col-league absorbed in the revenue setup. The Rule 5(1) will not allow that. Then what will be the position? An employee in spite of being senior to some junior employees will be junior to the employees who are junior to those junior employees.

43. Clause 4 of rule 5 states thus,

(8) একাধিক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে একই পদে দুই বা ততোধিক কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীকে নিয়মিত করা হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প যোগদানের তারিখের ভিত্তিতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে ।”

44. Good. But what will be the position if a junior employee is regularized before a senior employee and gets seniority over the regular employees appointed directly after his regularization. According to clause (1) of rule 5 the senior employees regularized after the appointment of those regular employees will be junior to them.

45. Clause 5 of Rule 5 states thus,

(৫) একাধিক উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে একই পদে দুই বা ততোধিক কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মাচরীকে নিয়মিত করা হইলে এবং তাহাদের যোগদানের তারিখ একই হইলে সেইক্ষেত্রে বয়ঃজ্যেষ্ঠতার ভিত্তিতে জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারিত হইবে।”

46. The same situation may arise as has been apprehended above for clause 4 of this Rule 5. Rule 6 of the Rules of 2005 also has made the rule 5 questionable. Rule 6 of this Rules of 2005 is quoted below;

(৬) উন্নয়ন প্রকল্পের চাকরীকাল গণনা।- নিয়মিতকৃত কোন কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীর উন্নয়ণ প্রকল্পে চাকুরীকাল তাহার বেতন, ছুটি, ও আনুষাঙ্গীক সুবিধাদি নির্ধারণের ক্ষেতে গণনা করা হইবে।

46. Obviously, this rule of 6 will create situations where the junior employees absorbed in the revenue setup may get much more pay and other benefits then the senior employees directly appointed in the revenue setup. This will create serious anomalies and other complications in the service.

47. However, in my opinion, the rule 5 of the Rules of 2005, in its present form, without any guiding clause, is not only a bad law for being the reason of creating anomalies, complications and discrimination etc. in the service, but also ultra vires the Constitution and as such void.

48. However, the authority, if wants to keep this provision i.e. computation of the seniority of the absorbed employees from the date of the regularization of their service alive then they can bring necessary amendment to this rule 5 by giving a short time limit to the Public Service Commission / Departmental promotion or Select Committee for giving their recommendations for the regularization of the service of the absorbed employees of a batch at a time, or, in my opinion, it will be better if the amendments are made to the effect that the seniority of the absorbed employees will be counted from the date of their absorption in the revenue setup subject to regularization of their service o obtaining necessary recommendation from Public Service Commission / Departmental promotion or Select Committee.

49. I endorse the view of the High Court Division that the Rule 5 of উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫ is liable to be effaced. But I am unable to endorse the view of the High Court Division that the writ petitioners are entitled to have their seniority computed from the date of their original entry in the Government Job.

50. However, from the above discussions, it is evident that in my opinion also the Rules issued, as quoted above, deserve to be made absolute hence, I dismiss these appeals.

Court Order
